Test Method: Potentiodynamic Polarization with exposed area of 1 cm2. Potentiodynamic polarization experiments were carried out using a scan rate of 0.1 mV/s commencing at a potential about 250 mV more active than the stable OCP. Before starting the polarization scan, the specimen in the sample holder (WE) was left in the cell for about 1 h to attain a steady state which is shown by a constant potential and current at the beginning of the experiment. The potcntiodynamic runs were programmed such that upon attaining a current density of 25μA/cm^2, the scan direction was reversed and the potentials were scanned back to the starting potential.

Before starting the polarization scan, the specimen in the sample holder (WE) was left in the cell for about 1 h to attain a steady state which is shown by a constant potential and current at the beginning of the experiment. The potcntiodynamic runs were programmed such that upon attaining a current density of 25μA/cm^2, the scan direction was reversed and the potentials were scanned back to the starting potential.
